When an app “ignores” audio focus, the other app no longer pauses it. Enabling it for the music app is usually enough.
Pauses itself when refused audio focus: enable the option on the other app instead.
Volume is applied to active streams; start playback in both apps to see the channels switch to “playing”.

Switch mode: this version of Android gives no access to per-app volume, so the fader switches sound on and off instead of fading it — music alone on the left, both in the middle, video alone on the right. A channel is muted below 40 %.
Nothing detected yet. The analysis needs a few seconds of music.
Average estimate for the piece, meant for playing along: quick variations are ignored. The family (which notes) is more reliable than the mode (which tonic).
Tap to see the history, one section per piece

1. Notes: the long-term average of the 12 pitch classes selects the family (which notes are used).
2. Chords: short frames are matched against triads. Pitch classes ignore octaves, so a chord is recognised whatever its inversion.
3. Loop: the music is compared with itself to find the period at which the chords repeat. Repetitions are stacked and averaged, which keeps the chords and fades the melody.
4. Tonic: the note where the piece spends the most time on the chord this mode builds on its tonic, backed by the bass line.
Numerals are read on the major scale of the tonic (♭VI, ♭VII…).

The sound — of the music app, or of the microphone when you choose it — is analysed on the device, in memory only. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere, and the microphone is never switched on by itself.
The 7 families and 33 “Scales of Harmonies”, their systematic names and the summary table are the work of Oliver Prehn (NewJazz). If this tool helps you, consider supporting him.

This phone does not let DuoMix Fader capture the sound of another app, as more recent versions of Android do. Choose a source below: “App sound” uses Android’s own playback capture (it asks for the recording permission, only to read the music app’s sound), “Microphone” analyses what the phone hears.
The music app is switched off under “Simultaneous playback”, and the microphone is off. Turn one of them on to analyse.
Listening through the phone’s microphone: its own speaker, a stereo, an instrument. It hears nothing of a headphone session. Nothing is recorded.
This version of Android does not give access to the players of other apps: per-app volume and the crossfader are switched off. Playing two apps at once still works.
OnePlus, OPPO and realme phones restrict adb, and therefore Shizuku. In Developer options, turn on “Disable permission monitoring”, restart Shizuku, then ask for the permission again.
The pieces you listened to, with their scale, colour tiles and chord progression. Scroll the list; tap to open the history.

Android lets one app play at a time and never lets an app change another app’s volume. Only the system, root, or the “shell” identity used by ADB can do that. DuoMix Fader asks for no root: it relies on Shizuku, a free open-source app that starts, through Wireless debugging, a small privileged service running as the shell identity — the same rights a computer gets when you connect the phone for debugging, nothing more. You start Shizuku yourself, you grant DuoMix Fader its permission yourself, and you can revoke it at any time.
What the privileged service does, and with which rights

The service runs as the shell user and accepts a short, fixed list of orders, only for the apps of the built-in catalogue:
• appops TAKE_AUDIO_FOCUS — an app stops being paused by the other (right: MANAGE_APP_OPS_MODES, held by the shell).
• Volume of each player of an app — through AudioPlaybackConfiguration, a system API (right: MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING).
• Sound of the music app, reduced on the spot to twelve pitch-class energies — an AudioPolicy with a loop-back mix (rights: CAPTURE_MEDIA_OUTPUT, MODIFY_AUDIO_ROUTING). Nothing is recorded.
• Title and artist of the current piece — its own media session (right: MEDIA_CONTENT_CONTROL).
• Close the notification shade and open DuoMix Fader’s own screen (cmd statusbar, am start).
• On Android 12: mute or unmute an app (appops PLAY_AUDIO), and allow DuoMix Fader itself to use Android’s playback capture (appops PROJECT_MEDIA).
It runs no arbitrary command, refuses any other package, and stops by itself when the app stops. The app has no network permission.

On Android 12 the shell holds fewer rights: it cannot reach other apps’ players nor capture their sound. DuoMix Fader reads what the shell is allowed to do when it connects, and adapts: the fader becomes a three-way switch (music, both, video), harmony uses Android’s own playback capture or the microphone, and the media-player card — which there shows only two colour tiles and shrinks the artwork to a thumbnail — is replaced by a notification drawn by the app. On Android 13 and later, nothing of this applies.
